task: Improve CVE detection, exploitability validation and unknown-vulnerability discovery
completed: Bound Strix run.json status, vulnerabilities ingestion, and persisted evidence to the same completed run directory.
Added regression coverage preventing cross-run artifact/provenance mixing.
Made active Strix scanner admission fail closed while its downstream runtime contract is not enforceable.
Exposed the Strix runtime-contract blocker through scanner capability diagnostics.
Added strix-execution-contract-v1 bound to job id, campaign policy fingerprint, normalized scope and exact request-rate ceiling.
Added canonical SHA-256 integrity and optional HMAC-SHA256 authentication using the existing audit signing key with domain separation.
Added a broker-bound request authorizer that rejects unsigned contracts, out-of-scope targets and request rates above the contract cap without performing network I/O.
Added redacted execution-contract trace metadata to Strix dry-run and result-ingestion events.
Added an admission-only Strix broker API that verifies a signed contract with a broker-scoped verification secret and performs no network I/O.
Placed the broker on an internal-only Docker network with no host port, data volume, Docker socket or Linux capabilities.
Added broker readiness, signed contract admission, wrong-key, out-of-scope, denied-host, rate-cap and unsafe-invariant tests.
Added CI coverage that builds the dedicated strix-broker Compose profile.
Added a separate read-only Strix egress service reachable from the broker but not directly from the scanner network.
Added GET/HEAD-only public-network egress with DNS resolution pinning, private/reserved IP rejection, TLS hostname preservation, no redirect following, bounded timeout/body and safe header handling.
Added actual per-contract request-start rate enforcement at the egress boundary.
Added double contract verification at broker and egress boundaries and preserved repeated response headers such as Set-Cookie.
Added three-zone Compose isolation tests and CI build coverage for both broker and egress services.
Added one-in-flight-request-per-contract enforcement on top of the signed RPS ceiling to bound slow-target concurrency.
Made broker readiness fail closed on the isolated egress service when the read-only proxy is enabled.
Merged PR #489 after CI, security and supply-chain all passed.
Added a dedicated Strix runner image pinned to official v1.6.2 Linux release assets with separate amd64/arm64 SHA-256 digests.
Pinned the v1.6.2 source commit ff5c8cc8e46d8e60c2bc2439f7bcb07c05ca3db2 and require the CLI to report exactly strix 1.6.2.
Added runtime re-attestation of the extracted Strix binary digest and fail-closed checks for Docker socket/DOCKER_HOST presence.
Added an inert non-root runner service with no ports, volumes or external network and active execution forced off.
Merged the live runner network proof and circular-import fix after CI, security and supply-chain passed.
Added xbow-remote-v1 registration through the Strix v1.6.2 runtime backend registry with bind mounts explicitly unsupported.
Kept the custom backend fail-closed: every backend invocation raises before any session or network operation.
Added CI verification against the official Strix v1.6.2 x86_64 Python wheel with its pinned SHA-256 and no dependency installation.
Added strix-runner-rpc-v1 with strict create/exec/resolve-port/delete request schemas.
Added HMAC-SHA256 request authentication with timestamp bounds, nonce replay protection, body limits and concurrent replay serialization.
Changed the isolated runner from an idle loop to an internal-only RPC service on port 8092 while keeping active execution impossible.
Added broker-to-runner readiness verification in CI without exposing a host port.
Surfaced RPC and standalone-backend-loading blockers through runtime capability diagnostics.

Kept the runner tmpfs noexec after CI exposed PyInstaller runtime extraction failure; moved exact CLI version verification to image build time and runtime re-attestation to the immutable manifest plus binary SHA-256.
Added a strict 5-second socket timeout and a 16-connection concurrency cap to the internal Strix runner RPC.
Exposed distinct Python-bootstrap and upstream Docker-preflight blockers in scanner capability diagnostics without blocking the Nuclei path.
Added a minimum 32-byte HMAC secret requirement for the internal Strix runner RPC, including signer, service, environment, CI fixture and documentation coverage.
Added a 10-second absolute runner RPC header/body read deadline and reject truncated request bodies before authentication or operation handling.
Added strix-python-bootstrap-plan-v1 that composes the attested v1.6.2 source, dependency lock and Python/uv toolchain without enabling patch application or execution.
The bootstrap plan identifies only check_docker_installed and pull_docker_image as patch candidates while preserving validate_environment.
Added strix-python-preflight-compatibility-v1 as a temporary context-managed patch that only replaces the two attested Docker preflight aliases in strix.interface.main.

The compatibility shim verifies exact patch-plan fields and direct import identity, preserves validate_environment, guards the upstream environment namespace, and restores all guarded symbols on every exit path.
Added regression tests for exact patching, tampered plans, import-identity mismatch, exception restoration, validation rebinding and upstream environment mutation.
Merged PR #525 after CI, security and supply-chain passed; the bounded Strix Python preflight compatibility shim is now on main.
Added strix-python-bootstrap-runtime-v1, which registers xbow-remote-v1 before importing strix.interface.main and rejects a pre-imported main module.
The prepared bootstrap revalidates backend registry stability, attests the exact preflight surface, builds the bounded patch plan and applies the compatibility shim only for the context lifetime.
The bootstrap keeps validate_environment intact and never invokes the Strix entrypoint; active execution remains disabled.
CI now exercises the bootstrap contract against the real pinned Strix v1.6.2 backend registry API while using synthetic interface modules so no scan is launched.
Merged PR #526 after CI, security and supply-chain passed; strix-python-bootstrap-runtime-v1 is now on main.
Expanded the pinned Nuclei discovery profile to include cve and vuln tags while retaining exclusions for dos, fuzz, intrusive, default-login and bruteforce templates.
Finding normalization now preserves CVE IDs, CPE, CVSS vector, EPSS score/percentile, references, scanner tags, verified-template state, declared max requests and vendor/product metadata.
Added bounded exact-template CVE recheck planning for verified Nuclei templates declaring at most five requests; existing scope, rate, sandbox and dry-run gates remain mandatory.
Added vulnerability intelligence that ranks known-CVE exploitability using severity, CVSS, EPSS, CPE, verified templates, KEV-like tags and evidence quality.
Added potential zero-day candidate scoring that requires no CVE plus high/critical severity, strong differential behavior and sufficient evidence/readiness; absence of a CVE alone never qualifies.
Unknown high-confidence candidates are routed to isolated-lab reproducer review and automatic zero-day exploitation remains disabled.
Finding intelligence now exposes known CVE counts, potential zero-day candidates, high exploitability findings and exact CVE recheck eligibility.
Changed CVE discovery to adaptive-by-default using Nuclei automatic technology-to-template mapping; broad mode explicitly adds cve,vuln tags and off mode retains only base discovery.
Added product/technology fingerprint correlation for known-CVE prioritization and temporal endpoint novelty as an additional unknown-vulnerability signal.
Propagated bounded CVE/CPE/EPSS/template metadata into the observation graph while preserving historical normalized finding IDs.
current_priority: Validate adaptive/broad CVE discovery, rich CVE evidence propagation, exploitability scoring and bounded exact-template rechecks through CI before merge.
blockers: Runner RPC session operations are deliberately unimplemented and always fail closed.
The official standalone PyInstaller Strix binary does not automatically import the Python xbow-remote-v1 backend hook.
A pinned Python runtime/bootstrap using the verified Strix v1.6.2 package is required before the custom backend can be selected by a real run.
Strix v1.6.2's Python entrypoint still performs Docker CLI/image preflight before scan execution even when a custom runtime backend is selected.
The bounded broker path supports only read-only GET/HEAD traffic, not the full method/tool surface Strix may require.
The upstream v1.6.2 Git tag object is unsigned; trust is anchored to the pinned source commit and official release-asset digests.
Contract v1 still uses symmetric HMAC verification rather than asymmetric verification.
safety_invariants: Fail closed on unknown scope or execution contract.
Independent validation remains required before confirmed findings.
next_steps: Run CI, security and supply-chain for CVE metadata normalization, vulnerability intelligence and bounded exact-template rechecks.
After validation, queue exact-template CVE rechecks as a dedicated provenance-bound validation job rather than a generic discovery scan.
Record recheck request/response artifacts and tie them to the original CVE finding without self-confirming the finding.
Add optional read-only CISA KEV/EPSS refresh ingestion so Nuclei-bundled intelligence can be refreshed without changing execution admission.
Correlate product/version fingerprints with CPE before prioritizing CVE templates to reduce false positives.
Keep unknown-vulnerability reproduction lab-only until a human-approved payload and impact boundary are defined.
